calls.prompt:
Company: SkyHop Airlines

US regional airline (~3,500 employees) flying short domestic routes from hubs in Denver and Salt Lake City. Fleet is 60 Embraer E175 jets and 25 Airbus A320-family jets (A319 and A320). Sells tickets online and at airports, charges bag fees, and runs its own maintenance hangar. Does not fly Boeing aircraft, Airbus A220/A350, or helicopters; no cargo-only flights, no international routes.

Rules that APPLY:
- FAA airworthiness directives for Embraer E175 (ERJ 170 family) or Airbus A319/A320, and their engines
- FAA rules for airline operations, pilots, crew rest and drug/alcohol testing
- DOT consumer rules for airline passengers (refunds, fees, accessibility)
- Airspace or airport rules at Denver or Salt Lake City, and airport fees charged to passengers
- TSA security rules for airlines

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Airworthiness directives for aircraft models we do not fly (Boeing, A220, A350, business jets, small planes, helicopters)
- Airspace changes at airports we do not serve
- Commercial space launches, drones, air-traffic-control equipment
- Banking, food, pharmacy, energy

Affected areas and owners:
- maintenance: Airworthiness directives, inspections, parts for our fleet → Carlos Mendez (Director of Maintenance)
- flight-ops: Flight operations, pilots and crew rules, airspace at our hubs → Jenna Holt (Flight Operations)
- customers: Passenger rights, refunds, fees, accessibility (DOT) → Omar Haddad (Customer Policy)
- safety-security: Drug/alcohol testing, TSA security, safety programs → Grace Liu (Safety & Security)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-06 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if it is a rule or proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-06, or a final rule that took effect within the 30 days before 2026-11-06; otherwise High for final rules, Medium for proposed rules and for notices with a deadline, Low for anything else), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

I found two documents in the 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06 window that affect SkyHop. The search tool can't list every Federal Register document for those dates, so other relevant items may exist, especially routine Airbus and Embraer ADs and ADs for engines.

## 1. Airbus A319/A320 overhead stowage bin AD (proposed rule)
- **Document number:** 2026-22587
- **Title:** Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22587/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes
- **Published:** 2026-11-05
- **Key deadline:** Comments are due December 21, 2026.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-06.
- **Owner:** maintenance (Carlos Mendez)
- **Reason:** The proposed AD covers A319-111 through -133 and A320-211 through -233 models. It addresses damage to the attachment points on overhead stowage bins from supplier ARIES. If not corrected, a bin could detach and injure occupants or block an escape path.
- **Action:** Check whether the A319/A320 fleet has the affected ARIES bins. Estimate the inspection and on-condition costs, and file comments with the FAA by December 21, 2026 if needed.

## 2. Passenger Facility Charge regulations (supplemental proposed rule)
- **Document number:** 2026-22450
- **Title:** Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations
- **URL:** https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22450 (short link; I built it from the document number)
- **Published:** 2026-11-04
- **Key deadline:** Comments are due January 4, 2027.
- **Tier:** Critical. It is a proposed rule with a deadline less than 90 days after 2026-11-06.
- **Owner:** customers (Omar Haddad)
- **Reason:** This is a supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking from the FAA that would change the PFC rules in 14 CFR Part 158. PFCs are airport fees added to passenger tickets, and SkyHop sells tickets at Denver and Salt Lake City.
- **Action:** Review the proposal for effects on how PFCs are collected, remitted and shown on tickets at DEN and SLC. Decide whether to file comments by January 4, 2027.

## Reviewed and excluded
- **2026-22382 (Embraer AD NPRM, published 2026-11-03):** It applies only to ERJ 190-100 and 190-200 models. SkyHop flies the E175 (ERJ 170-200), so I left it out. Carlos Mendez may still want to confirm that the fleet has no ERJ 190 models.
- **2026-22436 (Privacy Act notice, published 2026-11-03):** It concerns a drone beyond-visual-line-of-sight system of records. Drones are out of scope.
- **2026-22496 (Pilatus AD, published 2026-11-04):** SkyHop doesn't fly Pilatus aircraft.
- **2026-22497 (airspace correction, published 2026-11-04):** It corrects a VOR airway description in the eastern United States. That area is outside SkyHop's hubs.
- **HHS drug-testing laboratory list dated 2026-11-02 (2026-22321):** A secondary source mentions it only in passing. I couldn't confirm its content or publication date, so I did not include it. Grace Liu may want to check it.

markdown:
# Regulatory triage — SkyHop Airlines
Window 2026-11-02 → 2026-11-06 · as of 2026-11-06 · 2 items

## Critical (2)

- **Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes** [web search — verify]
  - Check whether the A319/A320 fleet has the affected ARIES bins, estimate inspection and on-condition costs, and file comments with the FAA by December 21, 2026 if needed.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-21 (comment, quoted ✓) · Owner: Carlos Mendez (Director of Maintenance) · Areas: maintenance
  - 91 FR 69732 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22587/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes
- **Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations** [web search — verify]
  - Review the proposal for effects on how PFCs are collected, remitted and shown on tickets at DEN and SLC, and decide whether to file comments by January 4, 2027.
  - Deadline: 2027-01-04 (comment, quoted ✓) · Owner: Omar Haddad (Customer Policy) · Areas: customers
  - 91 FR 69511 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/04/2026-22450/update-and-clarification-of-the-passenger-facility-charge-regulations

votes.why: Plain-English steps for the maintenance director: check the fleet for affected bins, estimate costs and comment by a date.
Treats the AD as a proposal open for comment, stays on the A319/A320 fleet and makes no unsupported claims.
Covers the bin inspection and the December 21, 2026 deadline but never says the inspection is one-time.
Clear single task: review the PFC proposal's effect on DEN and SLC ticketing and decide whether to comment by a date.
Only asks for a review of possible effects; it does not claim a final rule or confirmed changes to PFC collection or levels.
Names the PFC proposal, refers to PFC collection and remittance on tickets, and gives the January 4, 2027 comment deadline.
It assigns three steps rather than one and uses the unexplained term “on-condition costs.”
It frames applicability as something to check and does not claim the directive is final or applies to Embraer E175s.
It gives the comment deadline but does not specify a one-time inspection of the overhead bin attachment points.
It asks for both a review and a decision rather than one concrete next step, and leaves “PFCs” unexplained.
It asks the owner to assess possible effects without claiming the proposal is final, changes collection or remittance requirements, or raises fees.
It gives the comment date but does not identify the supplemental Passenger Facility Charge proposal under 14 CFR Part 158 or say that airlines collect the fees from passengers.
The action uses plain English and gives the maintenance director a concrete, logical next step starting with checking the fleet.
The action stays consistent with the provided title, reason, and rubric and avoids claiming the AD is final or applies to E175s.
The action omits that the proposed requirement is a one-time inspection and does not mention overhead stowage bin attachments.
The action clearly tells the owner in plain English to review the proposal for ticket impacts and decide whether to comment by the deadline.
Asking the owner to review potential effects does not claim the rule actually changes collection or remittance or that it is final.
The action omits that this is a supplemental proposal under 14 CFR part 158 (Passenger Facility Charge) and does not clearly state airlines collect PFCs from passengers.
